narrative.overview:
Reading the world's news is like finding your way through an international airport. Every frame element (masthead, navigation, section headings, labels, the "why it matters" block) is a bilingual wayfinding sign: the reading language set bold, the other language set light beside or beneath it. Between the signs, the reading column stays quiet: a cool off-white ground, a white article panel, a hyperlegible text face at a comfortable measure.

The system is flat, square and high-contrast. Depth comes from the black sign panel against the light ground, never from shadow. Signal yellow owns a full-width band on every screen (the section gate band under the overhead sign, the footer's top rule) and is otherwise spent on action plates, code squares and hover highlights. Pages are complete without imagery; structure and type carry everything. The world is light-only.

It deliberately rejects the broadsheet default (hairline rules plus a serif display face) and the dark tech-lab look of the previous jendume identity.
keyCharacteristics: Black sign panels (overhead, "why it matters", section directory, footer) on a cool light reading ground.
A signal-yellow gate band at full page width on every page.
Six permanent section codes (1 to 6) in numbered squares, always paired with drawn SVG direction arrows.
Both languages visible in every sign; the active one struck forward.
Square corners everywhere, 1px / 2px / 4px rules, no shadows.

rules.name: The Band Rule
rules.body: Signal yellow occupies one full-width band on every screen (the section gate band); elsewhere it appears only as bounded plates, code squares, short bars and hover marks, never as a second large field.

rules.name: The Two Surfaces Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two surface families: black signs and light reading ground. A new component is either a sign (sign / signal / sign-text / sign-muted) or reading matter (ground / paper / ink / muted); it never blends them or introduces a mid-grey panel.

rules.name: The Bilingual Sign Rule
rules.body: Every sign-level label shows both languages: reading language in Signika 600 or 700, the other language in Signika 300 in a muted color, beside or directly beneath it, marked with its `lang` attribute. Reading text (prose, decks, descriptions) is monolingual.

rules.name: The Signika for Signs Rule
rules.body: Signika sets everything that orients; Atkinson sets everything that is read. Fact (prose) and interpretation ("why it matters") stay typographically separated by surface, not by face alone.

rules.name: The No-Lift Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow or translates upward on hover. Hover is a fill change (yellow to deep yellow, black to panel two), a growing yellow highlight bar, or an arrow nudging 4px in its direction.

dos: Do show both languages on every sign-level element, the reading language bold and the other in Signika 300, muted.
Do pair every section reference with its permanent numbered code square (1 Dünya/World through 6 Perspektif/Perspective).
Do use the drawn SVG arrow for direction (right for go, down for "you are here", up-right for outward), never a text glyph.
Do keep corners square (0) and separate with 4px / 2px / 1px rules according to their meaning.
Do place region and the "why it matters" block before the prose on articles.
Do use the yellow highlight bar (0.32em tall, grows from 0 to 100% width) as the hover state for linked headlines.
donts: Don't add box shadows, raised cards or hover lift; the system is flat.
Don't round corners or use pills.
Don't put eyebrows or kickers above headlines; metadata belongs in the label line under the title.
Don't introduce a dark mode or a second accent hue; Alert Red is reserved for the key-development tag.
Don't set headings, nav or labels in Atkinson, or reading text in Signika (blockquotes excepted).
Don't load fonts from third-party hosts; both families are self-hosted woff2 under the site CSP.
